verdicts.trueWording: none of my magazine articles have been reprinted anywhere
verdicts.note: Raw page ultan.org.uk/plant-engineering fetched (200, browser UA). Quote verbatim in Wolfe's closing written reply to Nigel Price; Wolfe prefaces it with a 'to the best of my knowledge' hedge the claim drops, and the framing paragraph ties the articles to Plant Engineering back issues.
Raw page fetched. Opening paragraph, byline 'By Nigel', 27 July 2013: Wolfe 'worked (1972 – 1984) as an editor for the technical magazine Plant Engineering'. En dash matches; every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: senior editor of Plant Engineering magazine from 1972 to 1986
verdicts.note: Raw page plantengineering.com/gene-wolfe-1931-2019 fetched (200). Opening line of Bob Vavra's obituary carries the quote word for word, so the 1972–1986 dating limb holds; the comparative limb is arithmetically wrong against the 1984 verified at index 630.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the arithmetic limb 'four years later than the terminal date Ultan's Library gives' — 1986 is TWO years after Ultan's 1984, not four

verdicts.trueWording: which was good and fun and taught me a lot
verdicts.note: Raw blogspot reprint fetched (200). Header confirms Lawrence Person, Nova Express Vol 5 No 1, Fall/Winter 1998, posted 25 April 2021. Quote verbatim in the Plant Engineering answer: 'I also got to be the Letters to the Editor editor, which was good and fun and taught me a lot of stuff'; the Plant Engineering limb is fixed by LP's question and Wolfe's 'on the staff of Plant Engineering magazine'.

verdicts.trueWording: He's been my principal editor over the years
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Q: 'Who are the best editors you've worked with over the years?' A: 'Oh, David Hartwell, obviously. He's been my principal editor over the years.' Hartwell named first and called principal editor: both limbs supported. Straight apostrophe on the page, as in the claim.

verdicts.trueWording: Damon Knight would have to come in second
verdicts.note: Same answer, next sentence: 'Other than David Hartwell, Damon Knight would have to come in second.' The 'after Hartwell' limb is explicit in 'Other than David Hartwell'.

verdicts.trueWording: at least three drafts, occasionally as many as 10
verdicts.note: Raw text file at gwern.net fetched (200), full Washington Post Book World piece of 30 January 1983. Paragraph 3: 'Every one of his carefully wrought stories and novels undergoes at least three drafts, occasionally as many as 10.' The 'every one' limb is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: buys some 25 free-lanced articles a year
verdicts.note: Same raw text, paragraph 2: 'There he edits, buys some 25 free-lanced articles a year, and writes a major cover story every few months', with 'there' being Plant Engineering Magazine in Barrington, Illinois.

verdicts.trueWording: writes a major cover story every few months
verdicts.note: Raw text fetched. The quotation and the 'for Plant Engineering' limb are verbatim and supported in paragraph 2. The concurrency with The Book of the New Sun is a reasonable inference from his seven years' writing overlapping the job, but the page does not state it.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the temporal limb 'while writing The Book of the New Sun' — the page reports the cover stories in the present tense of the January 1983 interview, when Wolfe says he has finished the first draft of The Urth of the New Sun and is at work on short stories; it never dates the cover stories to the tetralogy's writing

verdicts.trueWording: Until I mail a manuscript out I'm never sure
verdicts.note: Same raw text, paragraph 3, Wolfe in his own voice: 'Until I mail a manuscript out I'm never sure that I'm through with it.'

verdicts.trueWording: when he grew me from a bean
verdicts.note: Same raw text, paragraph on Knight: 'That's what I meant when I dedicated The Fifth Head of Cerberus to Damon in memory of when he grew me from a bean.' Both limbs — the dedication and what it commemorates — are on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: a mentor to many contemporary science fiction writers
verdicts.note: Same raw text, same paragraph, in Dirda's reporting voice inside dashes: 'In 1967 Damon Knight--a mentor to many contemporary science fiction writers-- published Wolfe's third story'.

verdicts.trueWording: Knight liked the story but not its double-column format
verdicts.note: Raw wolfewiki.com Stories.TripTrap fetched (200). Section 'A note about the writing of the story', quoting Contemporary Authors Autobiography Series Vol. 9. The second limb is the page's own continuation: 'asked me to break it up into conventional skips from astronaut to alien and back to astronaut'.

verdicts.trueWording: marked to show the points at which he felt
verdicts.note: Same section: 'Knight returned Trip Trap marked to show the points at which he felt the switches from one letter to the other should be made.' Every limb of the claim sentence, including 'from one letter to the other', is the page's wording.

verdicts.trueWording: I spent a couple of hours trying to improve
verdicts.note: Same section, next sentence: 'I spent a couple of hours trying to improve on them and found I could not...' — 'them' being Knight's marked switch points from the preceding sentence.
